question: Can the current Colima/Docker host safely admit a later Blender 5.2 linux/amd64 runtime canary while preserving the frozen B38 worker ceilings, an explicit infrastructure reserve, build-storage rollback room, host disk reserve and zero competing containers?

reasoning.memory: The VM must provide the frozen 8 GiB worker ceiling plus a separately reserved 2 GiB for the Linux VM, Docker daemon and filesystem cache; a cgroup ceiling is not a reservation.
reasoning.cpu: The VM must provide the frozen four-CPU worker ceiling plus one CPU of infrastructure headroom; a CPU quota is not a reservation.
reasoning.dockerStorage: Eight GiB of free Docker storage is a pre-build safety floor for the 384,441,228-byte compressed Blender archive, extracted tree, package layers, final image and rollback after a failed build; it is an admission policy, not a predicted exact image size.

frozenAnalyzerAttacks: lower the Docker storage safety floor

decisionRules.workerHostCapacityBlocked: all observations and decisions reproduce exactly, the four expected blockers remain, all 14 attacks pass and runtime operation count is zero
decisionRules.eligibleForB41Preregistration: every gate is ACCEPTED in a new clean attempt; this changes external state and requires a separately preregistered B41, not reinterpretation of B40
decisionRules.runInvalid: runtime, ancestry, preregistration, probe trace, policy, evidence self-hash or attack count differs

nonClaims: B40 does not start, stop, restart or reconfigure Colima
B40 does not launch Blender or create, run, build, pull, exec, prune or delete a container/image
The 2 GiB memory, one CPU and 8 GiB Docker-storage reserves are explicit operational admission policies, not Blender minimum requirements or measured exact consumption
An enabled qemu-x86_64 registration does not prove Blender compatibility, Eevee/EGL availability, performance or output equivalence
No containment or production worker claim
